author: Aloha State News
title: Maui County and Higashimatsushima City formalize Friendship City agreement
text:
Maui County and Higashimatsushima City formalize Friendship City agreement
Maui County Mayor Richard Bissen and Mayor Iwao Atsumi of Higashimatsushima City, Japan, formalized a Friendship City agreement during a signing ceremony at the Kalana O Maui County building on July 8. The agreement recognizes a relationship rooted in resilience, cultural exchange, and mutual support following the 2023 Maui Wildfires.
The partnership grew from the Kibou for Maui program, which connected Lahainaluna High School students with residents of Higashimatsushima after the wildfires. The program was inspired by shared experiences of disaster recovery; in 2011, Higashimatsushima lost 1,110 lives and still has 23 people missing after the Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami. Through Kibou for Maui, Lahainaluna students learned firsthand from a community experienced in long-term recovery and rebuilding.
“We are so moved by the compassion and generosity from the people of Higashimatsushima,” Bissen said. “Through this connection, Lahainaluna students have been able to learn from long-term recovery in Japan and see what is possible years after disaster. This Friendship City agreement reflects our shared commitment to hope, resilience, and building a stronger future together.”
“With the signing of this agreement, our two communities will work together to strengthen cooperation in disaster preparedness, disaster risk reduction, and community resilience,” Atsumi said. “We also look forward to expanding educational and youth exchanges, promoting cultural exchange, sharing knowledge and best practices in local government and economic development, and building a framework for mutual assistance in times of disaster.”
After the signing ceremony, Bissen presented his pen to Kaulana Tihada—a Lahainaluna student who traveled to Japan through Kibou for Maui—as a gesture marking continued youth engagement between both communities.
A Friendship City agreement establishes a mayor-to-mayor relationship intended to encourage cultural exchange as well as educational opportunities. For more information on these relationships or other international agreements involving Maui County, visit its Office of Public Affairs webpage.
